id: title:Gilbert09:fail fast when posthog can t impersonate a bigquery destination account

review.posthog_relevance: Adds exception handling and tests to the BigQuery destination writer to distinguish IAM impersonation failures from transient errors, supporting configuration error handling.
review.reason: Adds ServiceUnavailable and RefreshError imports and a constant string for impersonation denial, along with a parametrized test, to the BigQuery destination writer. This supports distinguishing impersonation failures from transient errors, which could prevent unnecessary retries. This is a substantive, bounded correctness and reliability improvement.
review.uncertainty: The actual runtime behavior and complete implementation of the exception handling and conversion are not fully demonstrated in the supplied observations; the score relies on the presence of the supporting infrastructure and tests rather than complete execution or broader systemic changes.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No tier assignment performed.

observations.behavior: Adds ServiceUnavailable and RefreshError imports, and DestinationConfigurationError, to the BigQuery destination writer and its tests.
observations.posthog_connection: These exceptions are used to distinguish impersonation failures from other transient errors, supporting the configuration error handling added later.

observations.behavior: Defines a constant string representing the impersonation denial error body, including the specific IAM permission and status.
observations.posthog_connection: This string is used to construct the RefreshError and ServiceUnavailable exceptions that simulate the impersonation denial, shared between REST and gRPC paths.

observations.behavior: Adds a parametrized test that raises RefreshError and ServiceUnavailable with the impersonation denial body, expecting DestinationConfigurationError.
observations.posthog_connection: This test validates that the writer correctly converts impersonation failures into a configuration error rather than a transient failure, preventing unnecessary retries.
